To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(i) the spectral functions are modified by the medium and that (ii) the modifications are strongly dependent on the local density and the local temperature.

(i) a time evolution of spectral functions is needed in transport simulations of heavy-ion collisions, (ii) a BUU-type model is capable of reproducing the experimental data on dilepton production in heavy-ion collisions at SIS energies, (iii) the inmedium modifications of the ρ and ω spectral functions are found to be small, (iv) a time evolution is needed in the transport simulations of heavy ion collisions to reproduce the experimental data.

the in-medium modification of the spectral functions can be large, that the in-medium effects are not necessarily correlated to the dilepton yield, and that the in-medium contributions can be of the same order of magnitude as the vacuum ones.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a microscopic description of the propagation of vector mesons and dilepton production in heavy-ion collisions at SIS energies.
a consistent description of the dilepton spectrum in terms of inmedium spectral functions.
the propagation of spectral functions and the production of dileptons in a hot and dense medium.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the dilepton spectrum in heavy ion collisions at SIS energies, in particular the low mass region, can not be understood without taking into account the medium modifications of the spectral functions.
the in-medium modifications of the vector meson spectral function are not negligible, and should be considered for a quantitative description of the dilepton data.
the in-medium modifications are not negligible but not dominant either, and that the dilepton production in the region of 0.3–1 GeV is not yet well understood.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the inmedium modification of the spectral functions can explain the observed dilepton enhancement in the mass range 0.3-1 GeV/c^2, but the observed mass dependence of the dilepton enhancement cannot be reproduced by our approach.
the dilepton invariant mass spectrum at SIS energies is dominated by the vacuum ρ and ω contributions and the in-medium modifications are not visible.
we find a significant inmedium modification of the ρ and ω spectral function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the inmedium modifications of the ρ spectral function are rather small.
a realistic description of the dielectron spectrum requires a careful treatment of both, inmedium modifications and vacuum contributions.
